newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro Disney sees no debt reduction soon.
newsitem.headline: Euro Disney sees no debt reduction soon.

text.p: Euro Disney chief financial officer Xavier de Mezerac said on Tuesday that the company did not expect to reduce its 15.1 billion franc debt in the near future.
"There's no plan today to reduce this debt in the short-term," he told reporters at a news conference.

He said the company was holding off on any dividend payment to retain cash for investment purposes or for an eventual debt reduction. He also said the theme park operator, 39 percent owned by The Walt Disney Co, did not plan to invest in new attractions at the Disneyland Paris theme park in the 1996/97 year begun on October 1.
"We need to demonstrate over a longer period that we can make profits before we make a dividend," he said.

De Mezerac said it would not be easy to show profit increases as the costs of a 1994 six-billion franc financial restructuring are gradually phased in following a debt holiday. "It's not easy to improve year after year, but that's our plan," he said.
Euro Disney earlier reported a 77 percent rise in 1995/96 profit to 202 million francs, its second consecutive annual profit, after drawing a record 11.7 million visitors.
